 Rockets vs. Nuggets prediction, props: Nikola Jokic to outduel Kevin Durant 
 By 
 Malik Smith 
 Published 
 Nov. 20, 2026, 6:00 p.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make New York Post a Preferred Source 
 Nikola Jokic of the Denver Nuggets shoots against Jabari Smith Jr. and Kevin Durant of the Houston Rockets on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, in Houston. 
 Getty Images

 The Nuggets host the Rockets for an NBA Cup game this Friday as both teams look to improve their standing in the group. 
 The Rockets are 1-1 in Cup games, the Nuggets are 1-0 and they each trail the Mavericks, who are 2-0 in the group.
 The Nuggets are short favorites at Ball Arena for their second meeting against the Rockets this season.
 Rockets vs. Nuggets prediction, best bet
 The last time the Rockets and Nuggets played, Denver suffered a schedule loss. 
 Coming off a neutral-site game in Mexico City, the Nuggets had their flight to Houston delayed by a day and didn’t land in the city until 16 hours after they were scheduled to arrive.

 The team canceled shootaround and listed the entire starting lineup as questionable before later clearing them to play before tip-off. 
 Even with all the disruptions, the Nuggets overcame a 19-point deficit in the third and only trailed by six points at the five-minute mark in the fourth quarter with a chance to cut the Rockets’ lead to four.

 They ended up losing by 10, and while there are no moral victories, there is evidence that the Nuggets are better than their record suggests.
 This time the Nuggets have the advantage of playing at home against a Rockets team that is playing the last game of its four-game road trip. 
 The offense is still a work in progress in Denver, as Nikola Jokic is not in peak form right now. He’s played well, but not in the dominant way we’ve become accustomed to seeing.
 More importantly, his supporting cast hasn’t yet found the rhythm that made the Nuggets special in the past, but I’m more encouraged after their win over the Celtics on Wednesday.
 Their defense has carried them over the past two weeks and ranks among the top 10 in that small sample size. The Nuggets will need to lock in on that end to slow down a Rockets offense that is scoring 121.7 points per 100 possessions, most in the NBA. 
 Kevin Durant #7 of the Houston Rockets brings the ball up court against the Denver Nuggets on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, at Toyota Center in Houston. Getty Images

 I’m buying the Nuggets as a top-tier player in the West and expect them to start to round into form now that we’ve hit the one-month mark of the season. 
 I’ll bet on them to win outright Friday.
 The Play: Nuggets Moneyline (-119, DraftKings )
